title: Hydration and hydration mismatches
description: Learn how React reconnects server-rendered HTML to the client and how to diagnose and fix hydration mismatches.

data.text: When a server renders React to HTML, the browser receives static markup. **Hydration** is the process where React attaches event listeners, reuses the existing DOM, and takes over without rebuilding the page from scratch.

During hydration, React walks the server-rendered HTML and builds the internal Fiber tree. It compares the server markup with what the client expects. If everything matches, React hydrates the tree and the app becomes interactive. If something differs, React warns about a **hydration mismatch**.

items: Reuses existing DOM nodes to avoid re-creating them
Attaches click, change, and keyboard listeners
Replaces static markup with interactive React elements

data.text: A hydration mismatch happens when the HTML generated on the server differs from what React renders on the client. Common causes include timestamps, random values, browser-only APIs, and data that changed between server and client render.

data.title: A common mismatch cause
data.content: Using Date.now() during render produces different values on server and client.

items: Move time-sensitive or random values into useEffect so they only run on the client
Use `suppressHydrationWarning` when the difference is intentional and harmless
Ensure server and client read the same data source at the same time
Avoid reading `window`, `document`, or `localStorage` during initial render

data.caption: How React hydrates server-rendered HTML and what happens on mismatch.
data.definition:
flowchart TD
    A[Server renders HTML] --> B[Browser receives static markup]
    B --> C[React loads JS bundle]
    C --> D[React walks DOM tree]
    D --> E{Markup matches?}
    E -->|Yes| F[Attach listeners and hydrate]
    E -->|No| G[Log hydration mismatch warning]
    G --> H[Client re-renders from root]
    F --> I[App is interactive]

data.title: Mismatches trigger full client renders
data.text: If React detects a mismatch, it may discard the server-rendered DOM and rebuild the tree on the client. This is slower than hydration and causes a visual flash. Fix the root cause instead of silencing warnings.

data.title: Key takeaways
points: Hydration reuses server HTML instead of rebuilding it
Mismatches occur when server and client render different content
Fix mismatches at the source rather than suppressing warnings
Keep render-time code deterministic across server and client
data.takeaway: If you see hydration warnings in production, search for Date.now(), Math.random(), or direct browser API usage in your render path.
